revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Production control and end-of-line test plan. Authored because the lifecycle-continuation view reported production and end-of-line test as a gap with zero records.

calendar_note: Every date in this record is synthetic and belongs to the hypothetical Project Northcell. No organisation, plant, vehicle, technician or recycler named here exists.
purpose: Establish that every item leaving the production line has been configured, tested and identified, and that an item that fails any test is stopped rather than shipped with the failure recorded. The failure this plan exists to prevent is the escape of a defective item into a pack, which no later activity can detect because by then the item is inside a pack that looks correct from outside.

in_scope: Incoming inspection of the components that end up on a safety path
Programming of the application, bootloader and commissioning tool
Calibration verification against the calibration specification
Functional end-of-line tests including the safe-state path
Records of what each station did to each item
out_of_scope: Pack assembly and pack-level testing, which the pack integrator performs

Any claim that a passing end-of-line test makes the item safe. An end-of-line test samples the item's behaviour at one moment; it does not establish a safety case and this plan does not present it as one.

procedures.action: Incoming inspection: verify the identity and the lot of every component that will be fitted to a safety-relevant path
procedures.acceptance_condition: Every such component's part number matches the released hardware configuration record and no unapproved substitution is present

procedures.action: Programming station: write the application and bootloader and verify each write by readback before proceeding
procedures.acceptance_condition: The readback content hash equals the hash of the released build; a write that does not read back is a line stop and the board is not retried silently

procedures.action: Calibration station: apply the calibration data and verify each value against the calibration specification's tolerance
procedures.acceptance_condition: Every calibrated parameter is inside its stated tolerance and the applied value resolves to a canonical parameter id

procedures.action: Electrical station: verify supply, measurement input range and the contactor driver outputs
procedures.acceptance_condition: All measured quantities inside their stated limits with calibrated measuring equipment

procedures.action: Functional station: exercise the safe-state path, the precharge sequence and the degraded-mode entry, using a simulated pack
procedures.acceptance_condition: Each exercised transition occurs in the expected order and the safe state is reached from the fault injection within the fault-tolerant time interval

procedures.action: Identification station: write the configuration identification and read it back
procedures.acceptance_condition: The readback string resolves to exactly one released configuration

procedures.action: Route on the combined result: any station failing stops the item and the item is quarantined rather than repaired on the line
procedures.acceptance_condition: A stopped item is quarantined with its failure record, and no station may be bypassed to clear an item
procedures.decision_point: Whether a stopped item may be reworked off-line or scrapped

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: Every station's expectation derives from the released configuration record, and station 6 verifies the identification that record defines
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: The line tests against a configuration that was never released, and an item that fails the real configuration passes the line.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: Station 3 executes the calibration specification this area produces
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: Calibration tolerances differ between the specification and the line and whichever is looser wins in practice.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The functional tests at station 5 exercise the same transitions the service class is trained on
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: The service class is trained on transitions the line never verified, or verifies transitions the service class was not trained on.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: Line records are the baseline a field event is compared against
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A field fault cannot be characterised against the item's as-delivered behaviour, so the event cannot be attributed to the item or to its use.

operational_authorisation_statement: This record is a fictional engineering artefact. It is NOT an authorised production instruction, it authorises no production activity, and no station described in it exists. No item has been produced. production_authorized is false.

evidence_state.reason: No production line, vehicle, charging site, workshop, fleet or recycling facility exists anywhere in this corpus. Master-prompt clause 2.5 forbids energising hardware and connecting to vehicles, so no step below can be performed by any means available here. The record documents the procedure and records that it has not been run.

limitations: Synthetic. There is no production line, no pack plant and no item. Every station below describes a facility that does not exist.

The 100 ms acceptance criterion at station 5 is the safety goal's own fault-tolerant time interval. Measuring it on a line with a simulated pack would demonstrate that the item reacts within its budget under test conditions; it would not establish that it does so in a vehicle, and this plan does not claim it would.

The safe-state reaction test exercises one reaction path. A line test that reaches the safe state by the main path and not by the independent path would pass, so the plan requires the independent path to be exercised separately. That requirement is stated here and has not been implemented by anything.
The plan assumes a simulated pack with the real item fitted. That assumption has not been validated and no such fixture exists.
Nothing here establishes that the item is safe. An end-of-line test is a sampling activity and a safety case is not a sampling activity.
